claims.title: Exact finite stochastic predictive-equivalence theorem
claims.scope: finite hidden records, finite future queries, and one declared categorical conditional law for every record-query pair
assumptions: one finite renderer state determines one conditional outcome law for every later query
fresh sampling randomness is independent of which hidden record produced a shared renderer state
zero-error law reproduction is required
nonclaims: records with identical full future-law tensors may be merged exactly
exact equality of finite declared laws is not an empirical claim about estimated probabilities

claims.title: Weighted stochastic query TV and KL decompositions
claims.scope: finite stochastic query families under one exogenous query distribution shared by the compared records
assumptions: the joint transcript retains the selected query identity
categorical outcome spaces are aligned within each query
KL uses the usual infinite-divergence convention when reference support is absent
nonclaims: the decomposition changes when query selection depends on the hidden record
weighted average accuracy is not worst-query accuracy

claims.title: Finite stochastic predictive packing-cover bracket
claims.scope: finite target future laws under weighted or worst-query total-variation distortion epsilon
assumptions: the lower-bound packing has pairwise distance strictly greater than 2 epsilon
the unrestricted predictor may use arbitrary admissible law centers
the constructive upper bound restricts centers to target laws in the family
nonclaims: the target-centered upper bound need not equal the unrestricted optimum
a packing lower bound does not construct an approximate renderer

claims.title: Constructive approximate single-sink cover-index network bound
claims.scope: one source, one sink, one finite stochastic future-law family, and one target-centered epsilon-cover routed through an integer-capacity network
assumptions: the source assigns each hidden record to one declared covering center
the network transmits the fixed-length center index
the sink can sample the center's conditional law after the query arrives
nonclaims: capacity below the implemented target-cover upper bound may still be feasible through arbitrary centers
the construction is not a simultaneous multi-sink stochastic network-coding theorem

claims.title: Exact arbitrary-center covering of finite Bernoulli laws
claims.scope: one-query finite Bernoulli parameter families under total-variation tolerance epsilon
assumptions: Bernoulli TV equals absolute parameter distance
predictor centers may be arbitrary Bernoulli parameters in [0,1]
the objective minimizes the number of fixed-radius intervals covering all target parameters
nonclaims: the greedy interval theorem is one-dimensional and is not promoted to general categorical simplices
arbitrary interpolating predictor laws must be admissible under the declared model

claims.title: Bernoulli one-state minimax predictive radius
claims.scope: one finite set of Bernoulli success parameters approximated by one arbitrary Bernoulli predictor
assumptions: distortion is total variation
the predictor center may lie anywhere in [0,1]
nonclaims: the midpoint formula depends on the one-dimensional Bernoulli TV geometry
one predictor state does not identify which target parameter generated the data

claims.title: Target-centered cover conservatism at the Bernoulli endpoints
claims.scope: target Bernoulli laws p=0 and p=1 at total-variation tolerance epsilon=1/2
assumptions: unrestricted predictor centers may use p=1/2
target-centered covers may use only p=0 or p=1
nonclaims: the example does not imply target-centered covers are always loose
an unresolved general packing-cover certificate is not proof of infeasibility

claims.title: Finite stochastic packing, target-cover, and routed network certificate
claims.scope: bounded finite stochastic families and integer-capacity single-sink networks enumerated by the repository
assumptions: exact packing and target-cover searches remain below their declared record caps
the route certificate uses the supplied network and the target-centered center index
nonclaims: bounded exact search is not a scalable optimization theorem
successful finite routing is not empirical evidence for simulation
